an4.192:1.1: “Monks, these four traits may be known by means of four (other) traits.
an4.192:1.3: “It’s through living together that a person’s virtue may be known, and then only after a long period, not a short period; by one who is attentive, not by one who is inattentive; by one who is discerning, not by one who is not discerning.
an4.192:1.4: “It’s through dealing with a person that his purity may be known, and then only after a long period, not a short period; by one who is attentive, not by one who is inattentive; by one who is discerning, not by one who is not discerning.
an4.192:1.5: “It’s through adversity that a person’s endurance may be known, and then only after a long period, not a short period; by one who is attentive, not by one who is inattentive; by one who is discerning, not by one who is not discerning.
an4.192:1.6: “It’s through discussion that a person’s discernment may be known, and then only after a long period, not a short period; by one who is attentive, not by one who is inattentive; by one who is discerning, not by one who is not discerning.
an4.192:2.1: [1] “‘It’s through living together that a person’s virtue may be known, and then only after a long period, not a short period; by one who is attentive, not by one who is inattentive; by one who is discerning, not by one who is not discerning’:
an4.192:2.2: Thus it was said. And in reference to what was it said?
an4.192:2.3: “There is the case where one individual, through living with another, knows this:
an4.192:2.4: ‘For a long time this person has been torn, broken, spotted, splattered in his actions. He hasn’t been consistent in his actions.
an4.192:2.5: He hasn’t practiced consistently with regard to the precepts. He is an unprincipled person, not a virtuous, principled one.’
an4.192:3.1: And then there is the case where one individual, through living with another, knows this:
an4.192:3.2: ‘For a long time this person has been untorn, unbroken, unspotted, unsplattered in his actions. He has been consistent in his actions.
an4.192:3.3: He has practiced consistently with regard to the precepts. He is a virtuous, principled person, not an unprincipled one.’
an4.192:3.4: “‘It’s through living together that a person’s virtue may be known, and then only after a long period, not a short period; by one who is attentive, not by one who is inattentive; by one who is discerning, not by one who is not discerning’: Thus it was said. And in reference to this was it said.
an4.192:4.1: [2] “‘It’s through dealing with a person that his purity may be known, and then only after a long period, not a short period; by one who is attentive, not by one who is inattentive; by one who is discerning, not by one who is not discerning’:
an4.192:4.2: Thus it was said. And in reference to what was it said?
an4.192:4.3: “There is the case where one individual, through dealing with another, knows this:
an4.192:4.4: ‘This person deals one way when one-on-one, another way when with two, another way when with three, another way when with many.
an4.192:4.5: His earlier dealings do not jibe with his later dealings.
an4.192:4.6: He is impure in his dealings, not pure.’
an4.192:5.1: And then there is the case where one individual, through dealing with another, knows this:
an4.192:5.2: ‘The way this person deals when one-on-one, is the same way he deals when with two, when with three, when with many.
an4.192:5.3: His earlier dealings jibe with his later dealings.
an4.192:5.4: He is pure in his dealings, not impure.’
an4.192:5.5: “‘It’s through dealing with a person that his purity may be known, and then only after a long period, not a short period; by one who is attentive, not by one who is inattentive; by one who is discerning, not by one who is not discerning’: Thus it was said. And in reference to this was it said.
an4.192:6.1: [3] “‘It’s through adversity that a person’s endurance may be known, and then only after a long period, not a short period; by one who is attentive, not by one who is inattentive; by one who is discerning, not by one who is not discerning’:
an4.192:6.2: Thus it was said. And in reference to what was it said?
an4.192:6.3: “There is the case where a person, suffering loss of relatives, loss of wealth, or loss through disease, doesn’t reflect:
an4.192:6.4: ‘That’s how it is when living together in the world. That’s how it is when gaining a personal identity [atta-bhāva, literally “self-state”]. When there is living in the world, when there is the gaining of a personal identity, these eight worldly conditions spin after the world, and the world spins after these eight worldly conditions:
an4.192:6.5: gain, loss, status, disgrace, censure, praise, pleasure, & pain.’
an4.192:6.6: Suffering loss of relatives, loss of wealth, or loss through disease, he sorrows, grieves, & laments, beats his breast, becomes distraught.
an4.192:7.1: And then there is the case where a person, suffering loss of relatives, loss of wealth, or loss through disease, reflects:
an4.192:7.2: ‘That’s how it is when living together in the world. That’s how it is when gaining a personal identity. When there is living in the world, when there is the gaining of a personal identity, these eight worldly conditions spin after the world, and the world spins after these eight worldly conditions:
an4.192:7.3: gain, loss, status, disgrace, censure, praise, pleasure, & pain.’
an4.192:7.4: Suffering loss of relatives, loss of wealth, or loss through disease, he doesn’t sorrow, grieve, or lament, doesn’t beat his breast or become distraught.
an4.192:7.5: “‘It’s through adversity that a person’s endurance may be known, and then only after a long period, not a short period; by one who is attentive, not by one who is inattentive; by one who is discerning, not by one who is not discerning’:
an4.192:7.6: Thus it was said. And in reference to this was it said.
an4.192:8.1: [4] “‘It’s through discussion that a person’s discernment may be known, and then only after a long period, not a short period; by one who is attentive, not by one who is inattentive; by one who is discerning, not by one who is not discerning’:
an4.192:8.2: Thus it was said. And in reference to what was it said?
an4.192:8.3: “There is the case where one individual, through discussion with another, knows this:
an4.192:8.4: ‘From the way this person rises to an issue, from the way he applies (his reasoning), from the way he addresses a question, he is dull, not discerning.
an4.192:8.6: He doesn’t make statements that are deep, tranquil, refined, beyond the scope of conjecture, subtle, to-be-experienced by the wise.
an4.192:8.7: He cannot declare the meaning, teach it, describe it, set it forth, reveal it, explain it, or make it plain.
an4.192:9.1: Just as if a man with good eyesight standing on the shore of a body of water were to see a small fish rise.
an4.192:9.2: The thought would occur to him,
an4.192:9.3: ‘From the rise of this fish, from the break of its ripples, from its speed, it is a small fish, not a large one.’
an4.192:9.4: In the same way, one individual, in discussion with another, knows this:
an4.192:9.5: ‘From the way this person rises to an issue, from the way he applies (his reasoning), from the way he addresses a question…
an4.192:10.1: “And then there is the case where one individual, through discussion with another, knows this:
an4.192:10.2: ‘From the way this person rises to an issue, from the way he applies (his reasoning), from the way he addresses a question, he is discerning, not dull.
an4.192:10.4: He makes statements that are deep, tranquil, refined, beyond the scope of conjecture, subtle, to-be-experienced by the wise.
an4.192:10.5: He can declare the meaning, teach it, describe it, set it forth, reveal it, explain it, & make it plain.
an4.192:11.1: Just as if a man with good eyesight standing on the shore of a body of water were to see a large fish rise.
an4.192:11.2: The thought would occur to him,
an4.192:11.3: ‘From the rise of this fish, from the break of its ripples, from its speed, it is a large fish, not a small one.’
an4.192:11.4: In the same way, one individual, in discussion with another, knows this:
an4.192:11.5: ‘From the way this person rises to an issue, from the way he applies (his reasoning), from the way he addresses a question…
an4.192:12.1: “‘It’s through discussion that a person’s discernment may be known, and then only after a long period, not a short period; by one who is attentive, not by one who is inattentive; by one who is discerning, not by one who is not discerning’: Thus it was said. And in reference to this was it said.
an4.192:12.2: “These, monks, are the four traits that may be known by means of these four (other) traits.”
